Confirmed symptom: GET / returns 404 (empty dir). Bare Pod with no owner, no Service. I need to add a second container. Pod spec containers are mostly immutable — you can't add containers. So I must recreate the Pod with the same name and additional container.

Constraint: keep the pod serving, existing config intact. Recreate the Pod via kubectl replace --force? Better: export the existing spec, add init/sidecar container writing index.html into /srv, delete and re-create.

Design: second container (regular container, not init) — "adding a second container that writes the page into a volume shared with the web server". A sidecar that writes /srv/index.html then sleeps. Since restartPolicy Always and containers restart independently, use a container that writes and then sleeps forever. busybox: `sh -c 'echo ... > /srv/index.html; exec sleep 3600'` — could use `while true; do sleep 3600; done` or `sleep infinity`. Busybox sleep supports "infinity"? Busybox sleep accepts numeric only in some versions. Use `while true; do sleep 3600; done`.

Also ensure it's a plain container named e.g. "page-writer". The task says "adding a second container" — regular container is fine.

Write YAML file, delete pod, apply. Should I preserve the pod? Recreating is required. Let me use kubectl get -o yaml, strip runtime fields, add container.

I'll construct clean YAML manually, preserving labels, securityContext, tolerations etc. Also preserve the projected volume (kube-api-access will be regenerated automatically). Design: second container (regular container, not init) — "adding a second container that writes the page into a volume shared with the web server". A sidecar that writes /srv/index.html then sleeps. Since restartPolicy Always and containers restart independently, use a container that writes and then sleeps forever. busybox: `sh -c 'echo ... > /srv/index.html; exec sleep 3600'` — could use `while true; do sleep 3600; done` or `sleep infinity`. Busybox sleep supports "infinity"? Busybox sleep accepts numeric only in some versions. Use `while true; do sleep 3600; done`.

The reported symptom is fixed and verified end to end. ## What I found - `app` was a **bare Pod** (no `ownerReferences`, no Deployment/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet, no Service) running one container, `web`, with `httpd -f -p 8080 -h /srv` and an `emptyDir` volume `shared` mounted at `/srv`. - Direct observation of the symptom: `wget http://localhost:8080/` inside `web` returned `HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found`, and `ls -la /srv` showed an empty directory (`total 0`). ## Constraint and change A running Pod's `containers` list is immutable, so the only way to add a container was to recreate the same Pod object with the original configuration preserved. I saved the original manifest to `/tmp/app-backup.yaml`, then replaced it with `name: app`, namespace `default`, label `app: app`, the **unchanged** `web` container (same image `busybox:1.37.0`, same command, same `http` port 8080, same `shared` mount at `/srv`), and the same `emptyDir` volume, adding exactly one second container: - `page-writer` (`busybox:1.37.0`) mounts the same `shared` volume at `/srv`, writes `index.html` there, then idles (`while true; do sleep 3600; done`) so it stays running under `restartPolicy: Always`. No other settings (security context, tolerations, restart policy, ports) were altered. ## Verification (fresh observations) - Pod is `2/2 Running`, `Ready=True`, phase `Running`; both `page-writer` and `web` report `ready=true` with `restarts=0` (re-checked 20s later — still `2/2`, `restarts=0,0`). - `/srv` now contains `index.html` (116 bytes), and `page-writer` can read it from its own mount of the shared volume. - Serving through the Pod's web server at the root path: `GET http://localhost:8080/` returns **`HTTP/1.1 200 OK`**, `Content-type: text/html`, `Content-Length: 116`, with the body ` ...

Hello from the shared volume

...` — previously a 404 against an empty directory.
